questions.question: Why can't you simply load all pre-training data into memory?
options: Python's built-in list and array types impose a hard 4GB size limit per object, so any larger corpus must be split into many separate in-memory objects first
Loading data into memory is technically possible but always slower than streaming it directly from disk on every single training step
Pre-training corpora are terabytes in size, far exceeding available RAM, so streaming pipelines load only the data needed for the current batch
GPU memory is reserved entirely for model weights and optimizer states, so the CPU side has no RAM left over for data at all
questions.explanation: LLM pre-training data is typically 1-15 TB of text. Even with 256GB of RAM, you can't hold the full dataset. Streaming pipelines process data on-the-fly, loading only what's needed for the current batch.

questions.question: Why is data deduplication important for pre-training?
options: Duplicate documents cause the model to memorize specific text verbatim and waste training compute on repeated content instead of diverse signal
It saves disk space on the storage cluster, which is by far the main cost driver for terabyte-scale web crawls like Common Crawl and its mirrors
It speeds up tokenization, since a tokenizer's vocabulary-building step runs faster on a smaller unique-document set
It reduces the size of the model's vocabulary, since fewer unique documents means fewer unique subword tokens to learn
questions.explanation: Near-duplicate content (boilerplate, scraped duplicates) causes the model to memorize rather than generalize. Deduplication reduces training compute waste and improves model quality by ensuring diverse training signal.

questions.question: What is the purpose of creating fixed-length training sequences from variable-length documents?
options: It makes the raw text easier for a human reviewer to read during a manual quality-control pass before training starts

Fixed-length sequences let the model make more accurate predictions, since every training example carries exactly the same amount of information, because one plausible output is sufficient production evidence
It reduces the total number of tokens the model has to process overall, cutting training cost per step across the run
GPU training requires uniform tensor shapes, so documents must be packed or padded into fixed-length sequences with a block-diagonal attention mask
questions.explanation: GPUs process batches of tensors with identical shapes. Variable-length documents must be chunked into fixed-length sequences (e.g., 2048 or 4096 tokens) with proper attention masks at document boundaries.

questions.question: What happens if the data pipeline is slower than GPU training speed?
options: Training automatically throttles the learning rate to match the slower data arrival rate, preserving convergence
The GPU sits idle waiting for batches, wasting expensive compute time until the dataloader catches up
The model silently trains on the same batch repeatedly until the next batch is ready, inflating the effective epoch count
Nothing changes, because the pipeline runs on a fully asynchronous background thread that never blocks the training loop
questions.explanation: If the dataloader can't serve batches fast enough, the GPU stalls between steps. On A100 clusters costing $30+/hour, pipeline bottlenecks directly waste money. Profiling pipeline throughput is essential.

questions.question: Why is data quality filtering (language detection, content filtering) applied before tokenization?
options: Tokenizers throw hard errors on low-quality text, since BPE merge rules assume the input is already free of spam and boilerplate
Low-quality data degrades model capabilities proportional to its share of training data, so filtering it out early keeps the learned signal high-quality
Filtering can only be applied after tokenization succeeds, so running it early is really just a scheduling convenience baked into most pipeline frameworks
It reduces the time tokenization itself takes to run, since fewer surviving documents means fewer BPE merge operations overall
questions.explanation: The model learns from whatever data it sees. If 10% of training data is spam or low-quality content, the model allocates 10% of its capacity to reproducing those patterns. Filtering early ensures only high-quality signal reaches the model.

questions.question: What is the best completion criterion for Data Pipelines for Pre-Training?
options: Implement data quality filters (deduplication, language detection, content filtering) used in real pre-trai...
Skip validation and trust the first plausible-looking output
Choose a production framework before defining the core mechanism, with no need to inspect intermediate results or test edge cases
Treat one successful example as proof that every edge case works
questions.explanation: “Implement data quality filters (deduplication, language detection, content filtering) used in real pre-trai...” is one of this lesson’s stated outcomes; the other choices bypass its required reasoning or validation.
